questions.scenario: The Flipkart Big Billion Days (or Amazon Great Indian Festival) sale just went live at midnight. What are you doing?

options.text: Wondering how they manage to pack and ship millions of orders overnight without everything turning into chaos.
Calculating the exact final price after combining the 10% SBI bank discount, exchange offer, and super coins.
Scrolling through the app just to look at the flashy sale banners, countdown timers, and cool product graphics.
Thinking about how much profit the sellers are actually making after giving such massive 70% discounts.

questions.scenario: You order Maggi and chips on Zepto or Blinkit, and it arrives in exactly 8 minutes. What blows your mind the most?

options.text: How the warehouse team found the items, packed them in seconds, and the rider navigated the traffic so fast.
How the app algorithm predicted local demand perfectly to ensure your favorite spicy chips were in stock.
The funny, clever push notifications and the mouth-watering food photos that made you hungry in the first place.
How the delivery app negotiated with local brands to buy items at wholesale prices to make a profit on quick commerce.

questions.scenario: Your class is in charge of running the food stall for the School Fete/Carnival. What is your main job?

options.text: Running back and forth to bring fresh boxes of Samosas and cold drinks from the storage room to the front counter.
Sitting with the calculator, deciding if a combo of 'Samosa + Frooti' should be Rs. 35 or Rs. 40 to maximize earnings.
Decorating the stall with bright chart papers, balloons, and writing the menu in beautiful, eye-catching calligraphy.
Going to the local wholesale market with a teacher to negotiate the cheapest price for bulk cold drink crates.

questions.scenario: You're taking a 24-hour train journey via the Rajdhani Express to your grandparents' house. What's your role?

options.text: Fitting all the weirdly shaped trolley bags, tiffins, and water bottles perfectly under the heavy train seat.
Keeping a mental count of how many snacks are left so you don't run out before the train reaches the destination.
Making sure your travel outfit looks great for a quick Instagram or Snapchat story at the railway station.
Taking charge of booking the tickets on IRCTC, managing the journey budget, and deciding when to buy station food.

questions.scenario: Your long-awaited Myntra clothing parcel finally arrives. What's your first reaction?

options.text: Checking the tamper-proof seal, the plastic mailing bag, and admiring how efficiently it was packed to save space.
Checking the printed bill to make absolutely sure the 'TRYNEW' coupon code was applied correctly to the final total.
Holding the clothes up to the mirror to see if they look exactly as stylish as the model's photos on the app.
Checking the seller's tag and wondering if returning the item will cost the brand a lot of money in reverse shipping.

questions.scenario: Your society is organizing a big festival (like Ganesh Chaturthi or Durga Puja). How do you help out?

options.text: Physically coordinating the tent setup, moving the heavy chairs, and making sure the prasad is delivered to the pandal on time.
Maintaining the Excel sheet of who paid the 'chanda' (donation) and balancing the daily expenses down to the last rupee.
Designing the digital invite on Canva for the society WhatsApp group and deciding the floral decoration color themes.
Negotiating with the local pandit, tent decorators, and caterers to get the absolute best package deal for the society.

questions.scenario: You are browsing Swiggy or Zomato late at night to order Momos. How do you decide where to order from?

options.text: I filter by 'Fastest Delivery' or 'Under 30 mins' because I want it hot and I want it right now.
I compare prices between three different restaurants, apply promo codes, and calculate the cheapest option.
I look for the restaurant that has the highest quality, mouth-watering photos of their Momos and a premium-looking logo.
I stick to top-rated, popular sellers because I know they maintain hygiene standards and have the best reviews.

questions.scenario: It's the 1st of the month and time to stock up on the monthly groceries (Ration). How do you approach it?

options.text: Lifting the heavy 10kg Aashirvaad atta and sorting the bags efficiently into the kitchen cabinets so nothing falls out.
Making a precise list, checking what dal is already in the pantry, and estimating the total supermarket bill beforehand.
Re-organizing the transparent masala jars and snack boxes so the kitchen shelves look incredibly neat and aesthetically pleasing.
Convincing your parents to switch from the local Kirana store to D-Mart or Reliance Smart because of better bulk discounts.

questions.scenario: A brand new, trendy smartphone just launched in India. What catches your attention?

options.text: Hearing that it 'Sold Out in 3 seconds' and wondering how the company will physically ship 1 lakh phones in one day.
Analyzing the memory variants (128GB vs 256GB) and calculating if the Rs. 5000 price jump makes mathematical sense.
Watching the sleek, cinematic TV commercial and admiring the beautiful 3D graphics on the product's landing page.
Reading about how the mobile company tied up exclusively with Amazon instead of selling it in offline retail stores.

questions.scenario: The school year ended and you need to get rid of your old RD Sharma and NCERT books. What's your strategy?

options.text: Packing them tightly in a sturdy bag and personally delivering them to the buyer's house on your cycle to save time.
Checking how much a new book costs, calculating a 40% depreciation for wear-and-tear, and setting a firm selling price.
Clicking really bright, clear photos of the books against a nice background to post online so they look almost brand new.
Talking to 4 different juniors, hyping up how these exact books got you great marks, and closing the deal with the highest bidder.

Logistics_Manager.title: The Delivery & Operations Ninja (Supply Chain/Logistics Manager)
Logistics_Manager.primary_match_text: You are highly active, organized, and love moving fast. You don't just dream about things; you figure out the exact physical steps needed to make them happen efficiently.
Logistics_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing massive e-commerce warehouses, tracking thousands of delivery trucks on GPS, ensuring Zepto/Amazon orders are packed perfectly, and solving real-time traffic delays.
Logistics_Manager.alternative_match_text: Your love for speed and organization would also make you a fantastic Event Manager, Airline Operations Chief, or Military Logistics Officer.
Logistics_Manager.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Science. Degree: BBA in Logistics & Supply Chain Management or B.Com. Next Steps: Pursue an MBA in Supply Chain Management or Operations.

Pricing_Analyst.title: The Discount & Data Wizard (Inventory & Pricing Analyst)
Pricing_Analyst.primary_match_text: You have a sharp, analytical brain. You love numbers, calculating value, and finding patterns. You are the genius who decides when the 'Big Billion Days' sale should happen.
Pricing_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Looking at massive spreadsheets to track what products are running out of stock, running algorithms to set the perfect discount prices, and maximizing the company's daily revenue.
Pricing_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your mathematical mindset means you'd also excel as a Data Scientist, Financial Analyst, or Chartered Accountant (CA).
Pricing_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce with Math. Degree: B.Com (Hons), BBA, or B.Sc in Statistics. Next Steps: Learn Advanced Excel, SQL, and pursue an MBA in Finance or Data Analytics.

Visual_Merchandiser.title: The Digital Storefront Artist (Visual Merchandiser / Catalog Designer)
Visual_Merchandiser.primary_match_text: You are incredibly creative and have a great eye for aesthetics. You understand what makes people click, buy, and fall in love with a product just by looking at it.
Visual_Merchandiser.day_in_the_life: Designing stunning sale banners for apps, choosing the best photoshoots for models on Myntra, and writing catchy product descriptions that make items go viral.
Visual_Merchandiser.alternative_match_text: If not in e-commerce, your creative vibe would make you an amazing UI/UX Designer, Advertising Executive, or Content Creator.
Visual_Merchandiser.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Arts/Humanities is great). Degree: Bachelor of Design (B.Des), BA in Graphic Design, or Mass Communication. Next Steps: Build a strong digital portfolio and master tools like Photoshop/Figma.

Category_Head.title: The Business & Brand Boss (Category Head / Vendor Manager)
Category_Head.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader, negotiator, and big-picture thinker. You understand the business world intuitively and know exactly how to turn a simple product into a massive profit.
Category_Head.day_in_the_life: Meeting with top brands (like Nike or Samsung) to sell their products on your platform, negotiating profit margins, and planning the strategy for entire shopping categories.
Category_Head.alternative_match_text: Your business sense and negotiation skills would make you a brilliant Entrepreneur, Investment Banker, or Corporate Strategy Consultant.
Category_Head.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or BA in Economics. Next Steps: Gain 2-3 years of work experience, then strictly aim for an MBA in Marketing or Retail Management from top B-Schools (like IIMs).
